search_log: Searched "The Book of Two Ways" Jodi Picoult excerpt and located the authorized full-prologue excerpt on the author's site and Penguin Random House.

Searched the title with point of view, first person, third person, narrator, and narrated in the first person; most results were summaries or unrelated works, but the Kirkus audiobook review identified Dawn's controlling voice.

Searched publisher and Google Books combinations for an interior excerpt; Penguin Random House exposed the same prologue and whole-book synopsis, while Google Books results did not provide a usable interior preview.
Searched for alternating narration and timeline structure; publisher material described two possible futures, but no credible source indicated sustained narration by a different grammatical person.
Opened the author excerpt, Penguin Random House prologue and book page, and Kirkus review before recording them; a chapter-summary page timed out and was not used as person evidence.
person_note: Dawn Edelstein is the participating first-person controlling narrator. The authorized prologue establishes her I-voice, the full-audiobook review corroborates Dawn as the novel's narrative voice, and numerous quotes from varied present-day, retrospective, domestic, Egyptological, and death-doula contexts independently expose the same narrator as I. Several passages briefly shift into story-specific you for interior or rhetorical reflection, but the research found no evidence that these form sustained autonomous second-person chapters; they therefore do not make the novel ALTERNATING. First-person speech without an outside beat was treated as dialogue, and no diagnostic third-person base narration appeared. The main limitation is that the authorized prose excerpt covers the opening rather than the entire book, but the broad quote coverage and whole-book audio evidence resolve that scope limitation.
